body:
Firstly, I wanna say that I went into this trip with a very neutral mindset, honestly just looking to have some fun as I had slept extremely well the night before and had the whole next day to rest.
The tripmitself  had a normal duration and overall wasnt very intense. Im used to this dosage and know it brings me to a good trippy point with some mild visuals and heightened perception.
During the come up, I unfortunately got into a bit of an anxiety loop, focusing on a feeling of throat tightness and pressure in my ears and head. It felt like they shared a single point of focus, if that makes sense. This sensation isnt new to me, probably tied to some underlying anxiety issues, but thats not really the point of this account.
At basically the peak of my trip, I decided to play some chill melodic music. Then I suddenly felt this strange urge to kneel by my bedside and keep my hands in a prayer position. Im not a religious person and have never prayed in my life, but out of nowhere I felt this burst of extreme happiness and peace about my life and purpose. Within seconds, all my usual hangups like worries about my job or what I should be doing were just gone. I felt complete peace with my existence, like that was all I needed to do for the rest of my life.
I felt complete peace with my existence, like that was all I needed to do for the rest of my life.
The moment was short-lived, maybe two or three minutes at most. I even had to stop the album and take off my headphones completely because it felt like I had just heard God itself speaking through me. I was honestly overwhelmed.
The rest of the trip went smoothly, even though the weird pressure feeling came back here and there and dampened the experience a bit. Still, I think this was a massively important trip because of that breakthrough alone.
Im still not sure how to integrate the experience into my daily life, other than the mental reset I felt. Ive started studying Buddhism, Christianity, and Islam, since this trip sparked a deep spiritual curiosity in me. I now feel like theres definitely something out there, even if Im not sure what it is.
I dont want anyone to take this the wrong way, Im not saying I have the answer to religion, but if what I experienced doesnt count as divine intervention, I honestly dont know what would.
